title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities, determined by the Company to be its Directors and those employees directly reporting to the Managing Director.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: Clearance sub-tier within Key Management Personnel; distinguished only for the identity of the approver (the Board, rather than the Chairman).

tiers.name: Managing Director
tiers.description: Clearance sub-tier for the hardship/exceptional-circumstances exemption; distinguished only for the identity of the decision-maker (all other Board members, rather than the Managing Director).

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's Annual Financial Report
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release of the Company's Annual Financial Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Half Year Financial Report
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release of the Half Year Financial Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's quarterly reports (if applicable)
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release of the Company's quarterly reports (if applicable)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may at its discretion vary the Closed Period rule by general announcement to all Key Management Personnel, either before or during a Closed Period; the variation is announced generally and is not stated to be confidential.

rules.detail: The policy regulates only buying, selling or exercising rights in the Company's own securities (shares/options on issue); it does not define a broader 'dealing' concept and does not mention derivatives or other financial products created over or referencing those securities.
Hedging is not named or otherwise addressed anywhere in the policy, and there is no distinction between vested and unvested holdings.
Monetisation structures such as prepaid forwards are not addressed.
Short selling is not named; only short-term trading (holding period) is discouraged, which is a distinct concept.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.
CFDs and other derivative products are not named or otherwise addressed.

Margin lending is not prohibited or made subject to any approval regime; its existence is expressly assumed by the exception permitting a secured lender to dispose of the KMP's securities on default during a Closed Period.
rules.evidence: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Granting a mortgage or charge over Company securities as security to a lender is contemplated without prohibition or approval requirement; a sale under that mortgage or charge on default is confirmed not to breach insider trading law even if the person then holds inside information.
rules.evidence: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: No general secured financing restriction or approval regime exists; the policy assumes such arrangements (margin loans, mortgages/charges) may exist and only addresses the consequence of a lender's forced sale.
rules.evidence: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: General (softer, 'should never') discouragement of short-term trading, with a carve-out for exercising options followed by a prompt sale; no fixed holding period or LIFO basis is specified.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company’s securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: Any Key Management Personnel (other than the Chairman) wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company’s securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman or the Board before doing so. ... any Key Management Personnel who (or through his or her Associates) buys, sells, or exercises rights in relation to Company securities must notify the Company Secretary in writing of the details of the transaction within two (2) business days of the transaction occurring.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: If the Chairman wishes to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company’s securities, the Chairman must obtain the prior approval of the Board before doing so.

carve_outs: exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter
short_term.evidence: Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company’s securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

exceptions.evidence: acquire ordinary shares in the Company by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to ordinary shares.
acquire Company securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class.
acquire Company securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders or securities of the same class.
acquire, or agree to acquire or exercise options under an employee incentive scheme (as that term is defined in the ASX Listing Rules).
withdraw ordinary shares in the Company held on behalf of the Key Management Personnel in an employee incentive scheme ... where the withdrawal is permitted by the rules of that scheme.
transfer securities of the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the restricted person is a beneficiary.

make an investment in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.

where a restricted person is a trustee, trade in the securities of the Company by that trust, provided the restricted person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the restricted person.
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer.

trade under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.
dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

exercise (but not sell securities following exercise) an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or convert a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right, or the conversion of the security, falls during a prohibited period.

exceptions.approver: Chairman or the Board (per the general clearance procedure)
exceptions.evidence: trade under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy.

exceptions.approver: Managing Director (or all other members of the Board if the applicant is the Managing Director)
exceptions.evidence: Key Management Personnel who are not in possession of inside information ... may be given prior written clearance by the Managing Director (or in the case of the Managing Director by all other members of the Board) to sell or otherwise dispose of Company securities in a Closed Period where the person is in severe financial hardship.

exceptions.approver: Managing Director (or all other members of the Board if the applicant is the Managing Director)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances may apply to the disposal of Company securities by a Key Management Personnel if the person is required by a court order, a court enforceable undertaking ... to transfer or sell securities of the Company, or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to do so.

exemption_authority: Managing Director (or, where the applicant is the Managing Director, all other members of the Board) may grant prior written clearance to sell in a Closed Period for severe financial hardship (a pressing financial commitment satisfiable only by selling) or exceptional circumstances (court order, enforceable undertaking, or other overriding legal/regulatory requirement), each exemption specifying a time period; separately, the Company may vary the Closed Period rule generally by announcement to all KMP.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to both the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company and its subsidiaries on issue from time to time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because the policy's scope is limited to buying, selling or exercising rights in company-issued securities and never mentions derivatives, hedging or margin lending as regulated activities, an OTC put/call with a bank falls outside its express approval and closed-period regime, though the bank should confirm this reading with the Company Secretary before relying on it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: lender default sale and insider law
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This gives unusually strong comfort that the bank's enforcement sale on default will not itself constitute insider trading by the executive even if inside information exists at the time, and 3.4(a)(xii) separately excepts such a sale from the Closed Period restriction.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (ie a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume of the shares of the Company on the ASX for the preceding 20 trading days) by a Key Management Personnel needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company’s legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unwinding or settling a sizeable collar by physical delivery/sale could cross the 10%-of-holding or 10%-of-ADV thresholds, triggering a mandatory pre-sale discussion with the Board and legal advisers, adding a step and lead time to execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Key Management Personnel (other than the Chairman) wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company’s securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman or the Board before doing so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: It is untested whether writing a call or buying a put (which does not itself buy, sell or exercise rights in ELS shares) triggers this approval requirement; the bank should seek company confirmation rather than assume the derivative legs are unregulated.

summary: ELS's policy is narrow: it regulates only the buying, selling or exercising of rights in Company securities by Key Management Personnel, requiring prior written Chairman/Board approval and notification to the Company Secretary within two business days, and it never mentions derivatives, hedging, margin lending or secured financing as regulated activities. The policy affirmatively contemplates margin loans and share mortgages/charges: a secured lender's forced sale on default is excepted from the Closed Period restriction and is expressly confirmed not to breach insider trading law even if inside information is then held. With no vesting-state distinctions and no hedging or secured-financing approval regime, a funded collar over vested shares is not expressly prohibited, subject to the Closed Period windows (two weeks before to 48 hours after each results release), the general approval/notification requirement for any share-side dealing, and a mandatory Board/legal-adviser discussion if a resulting sale exceeds 10% of the individual's holding or 10% of 20-day average volume. Because the policy is silent rather than permissive by design, the bank should confirm with the Company Secretary whether the put/call legs themselves are treated as 'dealing' requiring approval before proceeding.
